Rarity.rationale: Strawberry.cs:11 is RelicRarity.Common. EXECUTED (b15-pool): Common in the transcribed grab bag, obtainable from any relic reward.

HasUponPickupEffect.rationale: Matches Strawberry.cs:13 -- and it is the only one of this batch's four AfterObtained relics whose C# declares it, which is correct: the flag exists so RelicModel.IsTradable excludes a relic that has already spent its effect (relics/base.py:132-136 mirrors that), and Strawberry is the only Common (i.e. otherwise tradable) one of the four. relic/small_capsule, relic/storybook and relic/tanxs_whistle are all Ancient and untradable regardless, and none of their C# files declares the flag either.

AfterObtained.rationale: Strawberry.cs:17-20 is `CreatureCmd.GainMaxHp(Owner.Creature, DynamicVars.MaxHp.BaseValue)` and CreatureCmd.GainMaxHp (CreatureCmd.cs:786-799) raises max HP and then Heals by the same amount -- which run.gain_max_hp reproduces line for line, citing the same source. MaxHpVar(7m) (Strawberry.cs:15) has no AscensionHelper.GetValueIfAscension in the file, so 7 is the pinned non-ascension value and strawberry.py:16's MAX_HP = 7 is right. EXECUTED (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b15.py b15-strawberry): a 40/80 player who takes Strawberry reaches 47/87. The relic's whole C# behaviour is faithful; the gap in this record is in the sim-only undo helper (guard G1).

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): `undo_after_obtained` (strawberry.py:21-25) CLAMPS instead of subtracting, so an un-granted Strawberry leaves up to 7 current HP behind -- contradicting its own comment
guards.issue: MECHANISM: after_obtained calls run.gain_max_hp(7), which raises max HP by 7 AND heals 7 (run.py:311-314). The undo calls run.lose_max_hp(7) -- whose own body is `new_max = max(1, max_hp - 7); hp = min(hp, new_max)` (run.py:316-321) -- and then repeats the clamp with `run.hp = min(run.hp, run.max_hp)` (strawberry.py:25). A clamp, not a subtraction: whenever the post-heal HP is at or below the restored max, the healed HP survives, and strawberry.py:22-23's comment claims it gives back 'the max HP and the heal that came with it'. EXECUTED (py audit/tools/relic_probes_b15.py b15-strawberry): from 40/80 the grant gives 47/87 and the undo leaves 47/80, i.e. 7 HP too high; from 50/80 -> 57/87 -> 57/80, same 7; only from 80/80 (where the heal was capped away) is the undo exact. SAME MECHANISM AND SAME VERDICT as relic/mango guard G1, which reached it by execution and whose issue text explicitly enumerates `strawberry.py:24-25 (7)` in its pool-wide list of all five implementers (binding rule 3, and PROMPT.md v6 item 3's second half: an undo_after_obtained that EXISTS and clamps violates its own stated contract and is a gap, distinct from the faithful ABSENCE of one). REACHABILITY (LIVE): the helper has no C# counterpart, but it is not dead code -- the conformance runner grants a node's relic and then swaps it for the one the save says was really picked, and it really calls it (verified by grep per binding rule 8: sts2_rl/conformance/runner.py:461 and :694), and relics/base.py:143-150's docstring names exactly this failure. Strawberry is Common in the grab bag, so any recorded run whose relic node offered it and did not take it reads 7 HP high for the rest of the run -- which is what DETECTOR 3's act-boundary HP assertion reports. Rule 7: leans on run.py, relics/base.py and conformance/runner.py, none hashed here.
